Our procurement team (contracts@aegishealth.com) asked for a redlined SOW and a simple change order PDF for signature. I attached our July usage export and a short note from finance explaining the reason for the request.

Can you confirm next steps and whether Redwood needs any additional approvals?

Soojin / Laura — I reviewed Aegis's note and Soojin's outline. Legal recommends the following approach to minimize downstream risk:

1) Credit mechanics: implement the price-offset as an "invoice credit" applied to the next three billing cycles, not a retroactive refund. The credit should be calculated pro rata based on the committed GPU-hours difference (40 -> 20) and capped to the total prepaid/committed amount for the period.
2) SOW edit: change Exhibit B to reflect reduced minimums and remove the phased integration line items tied to the delayed feature; add an explicit reversion date (2027-12-01) where commitments return to the prior minimum unless renewed in writing.
3) Change order language: include a short paragraph stating the change is temporary, the credit calculation formula, and a one-time administrative fee (if finance prefers) — keep the fee optional and documented.
4) Insurance / SLA: this adjustment does not alter SLA terms; include a short statement to that effect to avoid support confusion.

I've prepared a redlined Exhibit B (attached: AG-1452-sow-exhibitB-redline.docx) and a tracked change change-order draft. Two asks: (a) confirm whether Finance wants the credit as a line on the next invoice or posted as a standalone credit memo, and (b) confirm the effective and rollback dates (Soojin suggested 2027-09-01 to 2027-12-01).

If approved, Legal can fold these edits into the PDF change order for DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
